jobs.title: Principal/Staff HPC Network Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About San Francisco Compute

San Francisco Compute exists to give ambitious teams large scale supercomputers without taking on a catastrophic balance sheet risk. Most GPU clouds force you to sign long term contracts with no way out. If you underbuy, you miss the window. If you overbuy, you’ll blow up with no way out. It’s a desperate gamble that San Francisco Compute does not force you to play.

 

Originally, SFC was an AI lab that bought too big of a GPU cluster and was forced to sublease it or go under. Today, we build data centers and supercomputers, then lease those machines on contracts that let our customers sublease. More than anyone else in the industry, we deeply felt the pain and fear of being forced to bet the farm with your neocloud vendor. To enable subleasing, we invented the first compute market and became the first to offer physical settlement. That means we operate GPU clusters like a neocloud and derisk our customers like a market.

 

Customers buying GPU clusters don’t want to work through a network of brokers. They want to transact with the folks that have the keys to the cluster and can own the SLA.

 

To keep the industry safe from unnecessary risk, SFC needs to scale fast. To do that, we serve financially motivated parties as a technical partner to build, operate, & lease supercomputers on their behalf. Basically, we help folks who want an economic return build GPU clusters on their balance sheet, but operated in full by us. That lets us retain the technical control needed to run a cloud while scaling fast like a market. SFC’s ability to offer subleasing can significantly increase the levered returns for cluster owners.

 

Our hybrid model outperforms brokered contracts or other “compute markets,” which have to go through a network of counterparties to solve problems. It also lets us design custom solutions for our customers, like clusters deployed in regions next to your dataset or physical eval set or a large CPU fleet deployed colocated with your GPU cluster.

 

Our team includes senior & technical leadership from places like Lambda, Crusoe, Digital Ocean, AWS, and Hut8. Our CTO is the cofounder and former CEO of Voltage Park. In prior roles, our team has deployed 8GW of datacenter capacity & hundreds of thousands of GPUs. We’ve been described as having “the highest talent density in the space.” If you are an honorable, gritty person with eyes wide open & good epistemics, who wants to see AI go right, we’d love to work with you.

There has never been a more critical moment in history and it is up to us to shape it on behalf of those who come after us.

About the Role

GPU clusters are some of the most performant computers on the planet. Even smaller clusters by today’s standards would have ranked in the TOP500 five years ago. Our infrastructure team is responsible for architecting and deploying new clusters around the world and keeping them running smoothly. You’ll participate in on-call rotation, fix issues when they arise, and lean into automation to enable deployments at scale. We’re a small but ambitious team so you’ll be an early contributor helping to shape culture, mentor junior engineers, and learn from our customers.

About You

  • You will have 10+ years of experience with hands-on management or architecture with network for at least one GPU cluster in the past (ideally a cluster with >1k GPU’s but not required)

  • You deeply understand the fundamentals of Ethernet (RoCEv2) and/or InfiniBand networks in CLOS/fat-tree topologies

  • You have built HPC network architectures (eBGP, fat-tree, VXLAN, MCLAG, etc.)

  • The idea of implementing zero-touch provisioning for a large multi-layer network excites you (you embrace automation)

  • You appreciate, value and generate good documentation

  • You have the ability and willingness to mentor junior engineers

  • You’re open to coming in to our San Francisco office 3-4 days per week

Some Nice to Haves

  • You understand data center concepts including power, cooling and how to engage with colo providers

  • You have experience with Linux systems administration including managing kernel drivers and tuning the network stack

  • You have experience with Linux virtualization (KVM, QEMU, libvirt, etc.)

  • You’ve had exposure to containers and Kubernetes operators

Benefits

Generous equity grant

Team members are offered a competitive salary along with equity in the company

Visa Sponsorships

Yes, we sponsor visas and work permits

Retirement matching

We match 401(k) plans up to 4%

Medical, dental & vision

We offer highly competitive medical, dental, vision insurance for employees and dependents.

Time off

We offer unlimited paid time off as well as 10+ observed holidays

Parental leave

We offer biological, adoptive, and foster parents paid time off to spend quality time with family

Daily lunch

We cover lunch daily for employees

Unlimited office book budget

You can buy as many books for the office as you want

The San Francisco Compute Company is committed to maintaining a workplace free from discrimination and harassment.

We make employment decisions based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, belief, national origin, social or ethical origin, age, physical, mental, or sensory disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, civil union or domestic partnership status, past or present military service, HIV status, family medical history or genetic information, family or parental status including pregnancy, or any other status protected by law.

We welcome the opportunity to consider qualified applicants with prior arrest or conviction records. Our commitment to diversity includes hiring talented individuals regardless of their criminal history, in accordance with local, state, and federal laws, including San Francisco’s Fair Chance Ordinance and California’s ban-the-box laws.

We’re hiring a Compute Partnerships Manager. This role is based out of our San Francisco office, five days a week. The position is a client-facing, high-ownership role for someone who can navigate ambiguity, build relationships, and take operationally complex deals from initial conversation through delivery.

This is not a back-office procurement role. You will work directly with partners and internal teams to unlock capacity, move deals forward, and solve the practical issues that arise when deploying supercomputing infrastructure.

What You Will Do

Provider Intake & Supply Management

  • Source and onboard new GPU providers, securing additional compute capacity and diversifying our supply base

  • Run first-touch intake calls with prospective GPU providers, gathering hardware specs, pricing, and availability

  • Help vet incoming BOMs against SFC's cluster requirements, flagging gaps or non-standard components

  • Keep provider profiles and capacity trackers current as new information comes in

Contract Triage & Follow-Up

  • Track contracts through redline, review, and signature stages, flagging where things are stuck

  • Maintain a clear log of open items, owners, and deadlines across the contract pipeline

  • Work across supply, go-to-market, engineering, legal, and operations to move opportunities from prospect to signed agreement.

  • Own the details needed to bring capacity online: timelines, dependencies, escalation paths, and partner communication.

Pipeline Organization & Reporting

  • Own deal tracking, pipeline reporting, and CRM hygiene

  • Run tight weekly reporting on pipeline stages and blockers

  • Draft and maintain marketing collateral for providers: one-pagers, proposals, flyers, and decks

Account Mapping & Sales Enablement

  • Map accounts and identify new prospective partners across datacenters, GPU operators, and financing groups interested in compute investment

  • Draft and maintain marketing collateral for providers: one-pagers, proposals, flyers, and decks

Minimum Qualifications

  • 2–4 years in partnerships, deal desk, BD, or a similar coordination-heavy role, preferably in B2B infrastructure, cloud, or marketplace businesses

  • Pre-existing network across datacenter operators, neoclouds, or hyperscalers

  • Detail-oriented, comfortable owning a high volume of contracts, follow-ups, and trackers without things slipping

  • Exceptional communication and negotiation skills

  • High ownership and bias to action

Preferred Qualifications

  • Exposure to AI/ML workloads or GPU hardware specs

  • Experience with contract redlining or deal desk workflows

  • Comfortable reading a BOM or technical spec sheet

  • Worked closely with technical or legal teams, even if not an expert in either

What this role is not

  • It is not a traditional account-executive role.

  • It is not a narrowly scoped procurement or back-office operations role.

  • It is not a people-management role on day one.

Benefits

Generous equity grant

Team members are offered a competitive salary along with equity in the company

Visa Sponsorships

Yes, we sponsor visas and work permits

Retirement matching

We match 401(k) plans up to 4%

Medical, dental & vision

We offer highly competitive medical, dental, vision insurance for employees and dependents.

Time off

We offer unlimited paid time off as well as 10+ observed holidays

jobs.title: Commercial Counsel
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About San Francisco Compute

San Francisco Compute exists to give ambitious teams large scale supercomputers without taking on a catastrophic balance sheet risk. Most GPU clouds force you to sign long term contracts with no way out. If you underbuy, you miss the window. If you overbuy, you’ll blow up with no way out. It’s a desperate gamble that San Francisco Compute does not force you to play.

 

Originally, SFC was an AI lab that bought too big of a GPU cluster and was forced to sublease it or go under. Today, we build data centers and supercomputers, then lease those machines on contracts that let our customers sublease. More than anyone else in the industry, we deeply felt the pain and fear of being forced to bet the farm with your neocloud vendor. To enable subleasing, we invented the first compute market and became the first to offer physical settlement. That means we operate GPU clusters like a neocloud and derisk our customers like a market.

 

Customers buying GPU clusters don’t want to work through a network of brokers. They want to transact with the folks that have the keys to the cluster and can own the SLA.

 

To keep the industry safe from unnecessary risk, SFC needs to scale fast. To do that, we serve financially motivated parties as a technical partner to build, operate, & lease supercomputers on their behalf. Basically, we help folks who want an economic return build GPU clusters on their balance sheet, but operated in full by us. That lets us retain the technical control needed to run a cloud while scaling fast like a market. SFC’s ability to offer subleasing can significantly increase the levered returns for cluster owners.

 

Our hybrid model outperforms brokered contracts or other “compute markets,” which have to go through a network of counterparties to solve problems. It also lets us design custom solutions for our customers, like clusters deployed in regions next to your dataset or physical eval set or a large CPU fleet deployed colocated with your GPU cluster.

 

Our team includes senior & technical leadership from places like Lambda, Crusoe, Digital Ocean, AWS, and Hut8. Our CTO is the cofounder and former CEO of Voltage Park. In prior roles, our team has deployed 8GW of datacenter capacity & hundreds of thousands of GPUs. We’ve been described as having “the highest talent density in the space.” If you are an honorable, gritty person with eyes wide open & good epistemics, who wants to see AI go right, we’d love to work with you.

There has never been a more critical moment in history and it is up to us to shape it on behalf of those who come after us.

About the Role

SF Compute is looking for a Commercial Counsel to help build and scale our commercial legal function as we grow our AI infrastructure business. This role will partner closely with Sales, Business Development, Finance, Operations, Engineering, and leadership teams to structure, negotiate, and execute high-impact commercial agreements that enable the business to move quickly while managing risk.

You will own a broad range of commercial transactions, including enterprise customer agreements, strategic partnerships, technology agreements, vendor contracts, and infrastructure-related deals. This is a highly collaborative role for a practical, business-oriented attorney who enjoys operating in ambiguity, solving complex problems, and building scalable processes in a fast-moving technology environment.

The ideal candidate combines strong commercial judgment with a genuine interest in AI, compute infrastructure, and emerging technologies. You will help create the legal foundation that allows SF Compute to scale responsibly and efficiently.

This role is based in our San Francisco office and requires working onsite five days per week. We believe close collaboration and in-person partnership are critical as we build the legal foundation for a rapidly scaling AI infrastructure company.

What You Will Do

  • Draft, review, negotiate, and manage commercial agreements, including enterprise customer agreements, master services agreements, vendor agreements, technology agreements, strategic partnerships, NDAs, and other similar contracts.

  • Partner with Sales, Business Development, Finance, Operations, and Engineering teams to structure deals that align with business objectives while appropriately managing legal and commercial risk.

  • Serve as a trusted legal advisor to business teams, providing practical guidance on contract strategy, negotiation approaches, and business tradeoffs.

  • Support commercial transactions involving AI infrastructure, compute services, data center operations, technology partnerships, and other strategic initiatives.

  • Develop and improve contract processes, playbooks, and frameworks that enable teams to move faster while maintaining appropriate controls.

  • Identify and proactively address legal, regulatory, privacy, intellectual property, and operational considerations impacting commercial activities.

  • Work cross-functionally with internal stakeholders and external partners to drive deals from initial discussions through execution.

  • Bring strong ownership and judgment to new and evolving legal challenges as the company scales.

    Who You Are

  • JD from an accredited law school and active membership in at least one U.S. state bar (California preferred)

  • 3-5+ years of legal experience, including experience at a leading law firm and/or in-house legal team.

  • Strong experience drafting and negotiating a broad range of complex commercial technology agreements.

  • Experience supporting technology companies, cloud infrastructure, AI, data centers, SaaS, hardware, or other technical businesses strongly preferred.

  • Ability to understand complex technical products and translate business objectives into practical legal solutions.

  • Comfortable operating independently in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with evolving priorities.

  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to build trusted relationships across technical and non-technical teams.

Benefits

Generous equity grant

Team members are offered a competitive salary along with equity in the company

Visa Sponsorships

Yes, we sponsor visas and work permits

Retirement matching

We match 401(k) plans up to 4%

Medical, dental & vision

We offer highly competitive medical, dental, vision insurance for employees and dependents.

Time off

We offer unlimited paid time off as well as 10+ observed holidays

Parental leave

We offer biological, adoptive, and foster parents paid time off to spend quality time with family

Daily lunch

We cover lunch daily for employees

Unlimited office book budget

You can buy as many books for the office as you want

We welcome the opportunity to consider qualified applicants with prior arrest or conviction records. You'll raise the bar for visual and interaction quality across our product surfaces, working closely with engineering, product, and design partners.   • Design and build the high-fidelity, polished interfaces in our product

  • Raise the bar for frontend craft, interaction design, motion, visual detail, performance under real usage

  • Partner closely with product and engineering to turn rough ideas into shippable, delightful experiences

  • Make sound architectural decisions for frontend systems that scale with the product

  • Mentor other engineers on design sensibility and frontend craft

  • Grow into broader product ownership, understanding customer needs, business context, and shipping end-to-end

Who You Are

  • You have strong design instincts, but prefer to build rather than only spec

  • You have strong opinions about product quality and can point to specific things you'd fix in products you use every day

  • You've shipped genuinely complex frontend components — whether the complexity was technical (performance, real-time data, animation) or experiential (making something hard feel simple)

  • You're energized by both the craft of building and by understanding why something matters to the business and its customers

  • Deep expertise in a modern JS framework: React, Vue, Svelte, or SolidJS

  • A track record of shipping interfaces with real visual and interaction craft — not just functional, but genuinely good

  • Staff+ level ability to operate autonomously and make good judgment calls with limited direction

Nice To Have

  • Experience shipping products end-to-end to external customers, and understanding how that work mapped to business goals

  • Startup or early-stage experience, where you had to wear a product-thinking hat as well as an engineering one

  • Experience in developer tools, infrastructure, or technically dense product spaces

Customer-Facing Support

  • Own inbound support tickets and live escalations for enterprise customers running workloads on our GPU/AI infrastructure

  • Triage and resolve technical issues across compute, networking, and platform layers, spanning both scheduling/orchestration problems and performance issues

  • Communicate clearly with technical customers under pressure - set expectations, give real status updates, close the loop

  • Hand off cleanly across timezones so customers never feel the seams of follow-the-sun coverage

Technical Troubleshooting & Escalation

  • Use monitoring and alerting tools to diagnose issues before or as customers report them

  • Escalate hardware, data-center, or facility-level issues to the right internal or external party (engineering, colo partners, hardware OEMs) with a clear, well-documented handoff

  • Serve as a first responder on incidents, working alongside engineering through to resolution

Process & Tooling

  • Work from and help improve runbooks, SOPs, and the knowledge base - flag gaps, don't just work around them

  • Use AI-assisted tooling to work faster without losing quality or judgment

  • Track and care about your own CSAT, first-response, and time-to-resolve numbers - these aren't just manager metrics, they're your feedback loop

About You

  • 3-5 years in technical support, customer support engineering, or a similar customer-facing technical role

  • Comfortable troubleshooting infrastructure-level issues - Linux administration, basic shell or Python scripting, and hands-on use of monitoring/observability tools (e.g. Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog); GPU/AI/HPC experience is a strong plus, not a requirement

  • Can explain technical problems clearly to both technical customers and internal engineering teams

  • Calm under pressure - you don't rattle when a customer is frustrated or a system is down

  • Comfortable working shift-based hours as part of a 24/7 global coverage model, including occasional after-hours, weekend, or holiday coverage during incidents

  • Genuinely care about getting the customer to a good outcome, not just closing the ticket

  • Excited to help build process and coverage from scratch, not just operate inside an existing one

  • Excellent written communication skills, to both customers and internal teams

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with GPU/AI infrastructure, specialized hardware, or managed services

ABOUT SAN FRANCISCO COMPUTE

San Francisco Compute exists to give ambitious teams large scale supercomputers without taking on a catastrophic balance sheet risk. Most GPU clouds force you to sign long term contracts with no way out. If you underbuy, you miss the window. If you overbuy, you’ll blow up with no way out. It’s a desperate gamble that San Francisco Compute does not force you to play.

 

Originally, SFC was an AI lab that bought too big of a GPU cluster and was forced to sublease it or go under. Today, we build data centers and supercomputers, then lease those machines on contracts that let our customers sublease. More than anyone else in the industry, we deeply felt the pain and fear of being forced to bet the farm with your neocloud vendor. To enable subleasing, we invented the first compute market and became the first to offer physical settlement. That means we operate GPU clusters like a neocloud and derisk our customers like a market.

 

Customers buying GPU clusters don’t want to work through a network of brokers. They want to transact with the folks that have the keys to the cluster and can own the SLA.

 

To keep the industry safe from unnecessary risk, SFC needs to scale fast. To do that, we serve financially motivated parties as a technical partner to build, operate, & lease supercomputers on their behalf. Basically, we help folks who want an economic return build GPU clusters on their balance sheet, but operated in full by us. That lets us retain the technical control needed to run a cloud while scaling fast like a market. SFC’s ability to offer subleasing can significantly increase the levered returns for cluster owners. 

 

Our hybrid model outperforms brokered contracts or other “compute markets,” which have to go through a network of counterparties to solve problems. It also lets us design custom solutions for our customers, like clusters deployed in regions next to your dataset or physical eval set or a large CPU fleet deployed colocated with your GPU cluster.

 

Our team includes senior & technical leadership from places like Lambda, Crusoe, Digital Ocean, AWS, and Hut8. Our CTO is the cofounder and former CEO of Voltage Park. In prior roles, our team has deployed 8GW of datacenter capacity & hundreds of thousands of GPUs. We’ve been described as having “the highest talent density in the space.” If you are an honorable, gritty person with eyes wide open & good epistemics, who wants to see AI go right, we’d love to work with you. 



There has never been a more critical moment in history and it is up to us to shape it on behalf of those who come after us.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Customer-Facing Support

 - Own inbound support tickets and live escalations for enterprise customers running workloads on our GPU/AI infrastructure

 - Triage and resolve technical issues across compute, networking, and platform layers, spanning both scheduling/orchestration problems and performance issues

 - Communicate clearly with technical customers under pressure - set expectations, give real status updates, close the loop

 - Hand off cleanly across timezones so customers never feel the seams of follow-the-sun coverage

Technical Troubleshooting & Escalation

 - Use monitoring and alerting tools to diagnose issues before or as customers report them

 - Escalate hardware, data-center, or facility-level issues to the right internal or external party (engineering, colo partners, hardware OEMs) with a clear, well-documented handoff

 - Serve as a first responder on incidents, working alongside engineering through to resolution

Process & Tooling

 - Work from and help improve runbooks, SOPs, and the knowledge base - flag gaps, don't just work around them

 - Use AI-assisted tooling to work faster without losing quality or judgment

 - Track and care about your own CSAT, first-response, and time-to-resolve numbers - these aren't just manager metrics, they're your feedback loop
